institution.title: Institution review and filing
institution.intro: A frozen form goes to a licensed institution, which accepts or returns it and records the filing. The licence check is a demo, not verification.
institution.registry_empty: No institutions loaded. Nothing real ships with the product.
institution.load_demo_note: Placeholder names and licence numbers. They assert nothing about any real company.
institution.submit_note: The form must be frozen first. Submitting again switches institution and leaves the frozen form untouched.
institution.unknown_option: An institution not in the registry (see what happens)
institution.filing_note: The registration number comes from a human reading the government system. This product never generates one.
institution.creator_view_note: Switch the role to Institution to accept, return, or record a filing.
license.disclaimer: A demo check against local data. It is not licence verification and proves nothing about any real entity.
license.reason.not_in_registry: This institution is not in the registry, so nothing can be checked. Unknown, not approved.
license.reason.capital: Registered capital is below the demo threshold.
institution.load_demo_admin_only: Only an administrator can load the demo registry. Switch the role above to Admin.
wizard.platform_promoted: Platform will feature it (sponsor-promoted, or shown on a home or landing screen)
wizard.voluntary_key: Declaring it voluntarily as a key micro-drama
wizard.key_conditions_note: Either of these makes a project a key micro-drama on its own, whatever the investment amount — NRTA Circular 35 (2024).
flag.clause_not_yet_in_force: This result cites the Micro-Drama Administration Measures, which take effect on 2026-09-01. They are not yet in force.
filing.heading: Where this files
filing.pre_shoot.required: Required — file before the camera rolls, and film what you filed
filing.pre_shoot.varies_by_province: Set by your province; no province has published its rules yet
filing.document.programme_number: Programme number, issued by the platform
filing.blocks_release: You cannot publish until this is granted.
filing.no_block: The platform reviews this before broadcast; no prior government grant is needed.
wizard.budget_band: Rough budget, if you don't know the exact figure
wizard.budget_band.hint: Only used when the investment amount above is blank. An exact figure always wins, and only an exact figure gives a settled tier — a rough band is reported as provisional.
budget_band.band_a: Large — at or above the key micro-drama threshold
wizard.key_conditions_guidance: Leave both unticked unless you already know otherwise. Platform promotion is a commercial arrangement usually settled after the film is made, and declaring voluntarily is a choice to take the strictest route in exchange for a distribution licence — useful for awards, priority scheduling and negotiating with platforms.
wizard.domestic_platforms.hint: Leave blank if you don't know yet. This does not affect your tier or filing route today; it is recorded for the distribution check that is not built yet.
wizard.classifying.hint: Reading the logline against the subject rules. This calls a model and usually takes eight to twelve seconds.
help.unavailable: The model isn't configured, so I can only show the hint above.
help.logline: One or two sentences on what happens. This is what gets checked against the sensitive-subject rules, so describe the plot rather than the mood.
help.logline.example: An undercover officer infiltrates a trafficking ring and risks being exposed.
help.genre_keywords: A few words for the genre, separated by commas. Used alongside the logline when checking subject matter.
help.episode_count: How many episodes in the finished series. An estimate is fine — it does not decide your tier.
help.episode_minutes: Length of a single episode, in minutes. This decides whether the work counts as a micro-drama at all: twenty minutes or more and it follows a different path.
help.investment_amount_rmb: Total investment in RMB, digits only. This is the field that decides your tier, and only an exact figure gives a settled answer — leave it blank if you don't know yet.
help.budget_band: A rough bracket, used only when the exact amount above is blank. Any tier from a band is reported as provisional.
help.is_ai_generated: Tick if the work is AI generated. It matters more than it looks: AI micro-dramas have their own, much lower thresholds, so the same budget can land in a different tier.
help.is_ai_generated.example: 900,000 is the lightest tier for live action and the strictest for AI
help.platform_promoted: Tick only if a platform has agreed to feature the work — sponsor-promoted, or placed on a home or landing screen. This usually gets settled after the film is made, so leave it unticked if no deal exists yet.
help.platform_promoted.example: unticked, unless you already have the agreement
help.voluntary_key_declaration: Tick to declare the work as a key micro-drama by choice. It means the strictest route, in exchange for a distribution licence — worth it for awards, priority scheduling and negotiating with platforms.
help.no_clauses: The hint above is all the policy library has for this field. It comes from NRTA Circular 35 (2024), which isn't in the snapshot as a citable clause yet.
wizard.title: Working title
wizard.more_conditions: Two more things that can make it a key micro-drama
help.title: What you're calling it for now. It doesn't have to be final, but the filing form needs a title, so an empty one comes back as a gap later.
help.synopsis: A paragraph on the story. Read alongside the logline when checking for sensitive subject matter — more text gives that check more to find, and any match has to quote your own words back.
help.synopsis.example: After reuniting, one of them is drawn into an anti-narcotics operation and his cover starts to slip.
help.production_stage: How far the work has got. It matters because a key micro-drama must be filed before shooting starts — if you're already shooting one, you've passed a step rather than not reached it yet.
flag.filing_due_before_shooting: This is a key micro-drama, and those must be filed before shooting begins. You've already started, so this step is behind you rather than ahead — talk to your provincial authority about how to put it right.
